message.content:
Below is a quick‑start guide showing **how** to pull *only* the `id` and `context` columns for the CAA records belonging to `sample2.com`.  
I’ll illustrate it with two common patterns:

| Pattern | What it does |
|---------|--------------|
| **REST – “field selection”** | Most modern APIs let you pass a comma‑separated list of field names (`?fields=`). Only those keys will appear in each record. |
| **GraphQL** | You explicitly declare the shape of your result set in the query body. |

Pick whichever matches the provider you’re talking to. If neither applies, let me know the exact API name and I’ll tailor the solution further.

---

## 1️⃣ REST – Field Selection  

### Example URL

```
GET https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa-records?fields=id,context
```

> **Why it works:**  
> - `/v1/.../caa-records`: Endpoint that returns all CAA entries for the domain.  
> - `?fields=id,context`: Tells the server to include *just* those two properties per entry.

### Full cURL Command

```bash
curl --request GET \
     --url "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/v1/domains/sample2.com/caa-records?fields=id,context" \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer secret567"
```

#### Expected JSON Response

```json
{
  "records": [
    { "id": "caas_00123",   "context": "issue" },
    { "id": "caas_00456",   "context": "iodef" }
  ]
}
```

*(If the provider nests results differently—e.g., under `"data"` instead of `"records"`—the same principle holds.)*

### Things To Double‑Check

| Check | Why |
|-------|-----|
| **Endpoint path** | Some providers expose CAA records at `/zones/{zone_id}/recordsets/CANAME`, others at `/domains/.../caa`. Verify against docs. |
| **Field naming** | Ensure the API uses exactly `id` & `context`; sometimes it’s `identifier` or `ctx`. |
| **Pagination** | Large zones may paginate. Add `&pageSize=1000` or iterate over pages until no more items. |
| **Rate limits** | With many domains, hit the limit quickly. Cache responses locally when possible. |

---

## 2️⃣ GraphQL – Explicit Projection  

If your provider offers a GraphQL interface, you can write something like:

```graphql
query {
  caaRecords(domainName:"sample2.com") {
    id
    context
  }
}
```

Send it via POST:

```bash
curl --request POST \
     --url "https://api.yourdnsprovider.com/graphql" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer secret567" \
     --data '{"query":"{ caaRecords(domainName:\"sample2.com\") { id context } }"}'
```

Result:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "caaRecords": [
      {"id":"caas_00123","context":"issue"},
      {"id":"caas_00456","context":"iodef"}
    ]
  }
}
```

---

## Quick Checklist Before Running

| ✅ Item | How to verify |
|--------|---------------|
| **API base URL** | Look up the official documentation or console dashboard. |
| **Authentication method** | Header `Authorization: Bearer <token>` is standard; confirm token scope includes read access to DNS records. |
| **Parameter names** | Docs usually show examples; copy/paste them into your client. |
| **Error handling** | Expect HTTP status codes 200–299 for success; otherwise parse error messages. |
| **Testing** | Run a dry run first with a small page size to ensure output structure before scaling. |

Feel free to paste the above snippets directly into your terminal or adapt them to whatever SDK/language you prefer (Python `requests`, Node.js `axios`, etc.). Let me know if you hit any snags!
